```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, dpi = 150)
```

## What this version is for

The slide-deck version of the EAC map. It keeps the corrected pathway from
`kelp_EAC_map_v3.Rmd`: the current runs bold to the separation point, the
eastward branch takes the bold line and the arrowhead because that is where
most of the transport goes, and the southward extension is thin and dashed.
The eddy circles are gone.

What is stripped back is everything else. Type is enlarged throughout,
because this is read from the back of a room rather than off a page. The axis
titles are gone and the ticks are down to every eight degrees, since nobody
reads coordinates off a slide. The source note is dropped: on the slide it
lives in the footer, set in the deck's own citation style, where it is legible.

```{r libraries}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)
```

```{r load-sst}
# NOAA OISST V2.1, annual mean 2015. Keep the CSV beside this Rmd.
sst_mean <- read.csv("oisst_annual_mean_seaus.csv")

aus <- ne_countries(country = "Australia", scale = "medium",
                    returnclass = "sf")
```

```{r pathway}
SEP_LON <- 153.0
SEP_LAT <- -34.0

# the EAC proper: ends where it leaves the coast
eac_main <- data.frame(
  lon = c(151.0, 153.5, 154.5, 155.0, 154.5, 154.0, SEP_LON),
  lat = c(-22.0, -24.0, -26.0, -28.0, -30.0, -32.0, SEP_LAT)
)

# the Tasman Front: most of the transport, so this keeps the bold line
tasman_front <- data.frame(
  lon = c(SEP_LON, 154.5, 156.0, 157.6),
  lat = c(SEP_LAT, -34.5, -35.0, -35.6)
)

# the extension: the remainder, reaching Tasmania
eac_extension <- data.frame(
  lon = c(SEP_LON, 152.5, 151.5, 151.0, 150.5, 149.5, 149.0),
  lat = c(SEP_LAT, -36.0, -38.0, -40.0, -41.0, -42.0, -43.5)
)
```

## Figure

```{r sst-map-simple, fig.width=6, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Annual mean sea surface temperature along the east Australian coast (NOAA OISST V2.1, 2015). The East Australian Current separates near 34 degrees south, where most of its transport turns east. The remainder continues south as the EAC extension, carrying warm, nutrient-poor water to Tasmania."}

p_simple <- ggplot() +
  geom_raster(data = sst_mean, aes(x = lon, y = lat, fill = sst),
              interpolate = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours  = c("#053061", "#2166ac", "#4393c3", "#92c5de",
                 "#fddbc7", "#f4a582", "#d6604d", "#b2182b", "#67001f"),
    name     = "Mean annual\nSST (°C)",
    na.value = "white", limits = c(11, 27), breaks = seq(12, 26, 4)
  ) +
  geom_sf(data = aus, fill = "#d4c5a9", colour = "#8a7560",
          linewidth = 0.4) +

  # the current, bold to the separation point, no arrowhead yet
  geom_path(data = eac_main, aes(lon, lat), colour = "white",
            linewidth = 1.4, lineend = "round", linejoin = "round") +

  # the Tasman Front keeps the bold line and takes the arrowhead
  geom_path(data = tasman_front, aes(lon, lat), colour = "white",
            linewidth = 1.4, lineend = "round", linejoin = "round",
            arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.3, "cm"), type = "closed")) +

  # the extension, thin and dashed, with an open arrowhead
  geom_path(data = eac_extension, aes(lon, lat), colour = "white",
            linewidth = 0.8, linetype = "22", lineend = "round",
            arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.22, "cm"), type = "open")) +

  # marker so the separation label has something to point at
  geom_point(aes(x = SEP_LON, y = SEP_LAT), shape = 21, size = 2.4,
             colour = "white", fill = "white", stroke = 0.6) +

  annotate("rect", xmin = 143.5, xmax = 150.5, ymin = -40.5, ymax = -38.5,
           fill = NA, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6,
           linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = 146.5, y = -38.9, label = "Bass Strait",
           colour = "white", size = 3.4, fontface = "italic") +

  annotate("text", x = 150.3, y = -21.2,
           label = "East Australian\nCurrent",
           colour = "white", size = 4.4, fontface = "bold",
           lineheight = 0.9, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 152.2, y = -36.8,
           label = "separates ~34°S,\nmost flow turns east",
           colour = "white", size = 3.0, fontface = "italic",
           lineheight = 0.9, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 151.9, y = -42.2,
           label = "warm,\nnutrient-poor\nwater",
           colour = "white", size = 3.8, fontface = "italic",
           lineheight = 0.9, hjust = 0) +
  annotate("text", x = 145.0, y = -42.3, label = "Tasmania",
           colour = "grey20", size = 4.6, fontface = "italic") +
  annotate("text", x = 142.5, y = -37.5, label = "Victoria",
           colour = "grey20", size = 4.0, fontface = "italic") +

  coord_sf(xlim = c(138, 158), ylim = c(-45, -20), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(140, 156, 8),
                     labels = function(x) paste0(x, "°E")) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-44, -20, 8),
                     labels = function(y) paste0(abs(y), "°S")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    panel.background  = element_rect(fill = "#cde8f0", colour = NA),
    panel.grid        = element_blank(),
    plot.background   = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    axis.text         = element_text(size = 10, colour = "grey45"),
    legend.title      = element_text(size = 11),
    legend.text       = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.position   = "right",
    legend.key.height = unit(1.5, "cm"),
    plot.margin       = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  )

```

```{r save}
ggsave("kelp_EAC_SST_map_simple.png", p_simple, width = 6, height = 8,
       dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```
